subject: orthopaedics
title: Complex Regional Pain Syndrome

steps.tx: **Complex regional pain syndrome** (CRPS) is a disabling chronic neuro-inflammatory pain condition that develops after bone fractures, soft tissue trauma, or surgical interventions. The syndrome is categorized into two distinct clinical subtypes based on neural status: CRPS type 1 (historically termed Sudeck atrophy or reflex sympathetic dystrophy) occurs in the absence of a verifiable major peripheral nerve lesion. In contrast, CRPS type 2 (historically termed causalgia) develops in the presence of an identifiable major peripheral nerve trunk injury.
steps.say: Complex regional pain syndrome is a severe post-traumatic pain condition. Type one occurs without any demonstrable nerve lesion, whereas type two develops directly after injury to a major peripheral nerve trunk.

left.title: CRPS Type 1 (Sudeck Atrophy)
points: Follows minor sprain, Colles fracture, cast
Accounts for ninety percent of clinical cases

right.title: CRPS Type 2 (Causalgia)
points: Direct injury to median or sciatic nerve trunks
Pain concentrated in defined nerve territory

steps.tx: **Pathophysiological mechanisms** driving complex regional pain syndrome involve aberrant neurogenic inflammation, microvascular endothelial dysfunction, and central nervous system sensitization. Trauma triggers exaggerated antidromic axonal reflexes that release substance P and calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) into tissues, producing sustained vasodilatation and protein extravasation. Over time, pathological alpha-adrenoceptor upregulation on nociceptive C-fibres couples the sympathetic nervous system directly to pain pathways, creating sympathetically maintained pain accompanied by cortical somatosensory reorganization.
steps.say: Aberrant neurogenic inflammation releases substance P and CGRP, causing persistent redness and swelling. Later, sensory nerves sprout adrenergic receptors, allowing sympathetic activity to directly drive intense pain signals.

nodes.label: Tissue Trauma
nodes.sub: Fracture or crush injury activates nociceptors

nodes.label: Neurogenic Burst
nodes.sub: Excess release of substance P and CGRP neuropeptides

nodes.label: Sympathetic Coupling
nodes.sub: Adrenergic receptors sprout on sensory C-fibres

nodes.label: Central Sensitization
nodes.sub: Dorsal horn wind-up and cortical somatosensory loss

steps.tx: **Clinical triad of symptoms** characterising complex regional pain syndrome includes disproportionate continuous pain, autonomic vasomotor/sudomotor instability, and trophic tissue alterations. Patients report excruciating, intractable burning or aching pain that is entirely disproportionate in magnitude and duration to the inciting injury. Autonomic signs manifest as prominent limb swelling, temperature asymmetries exceeding one degree Celsius compared to the healthy contralateral limb, hyperhidrosis, and trophic changes including shiny atrophic skin, altered hair growth, and brittle grooved nails.
steps.say: CRPS presents with a classic triad: severe burning pain out of proportion to the injury, autonomic temperature and sweating changes, and trophic alterations like shiny thin skin and brittle nails.

vis.title: Clinical Signs and Symptoms Triad in CRPS
rows: Hyperalgesia to pinprick, allodynia to light touch
Skin color asymmetry, temperature gap >1 deg C
Joint contractures, shiny skin, brittle nails

steps.tx: **Budapest diagnostic criteria** endorsed by the International Association for the Study of Pain require continuing pain disproportionate to the inciting event, plus documented symptoms and objective physical signs across four sensory categories. A patient must report at least one symptom in three of four categories (sensory, vasomotor, sudomotor/edema, motor/trophic), and the clinician must objectively demonstrate at least one sign in two of the four categories on physical examination, with no other diagnosis explaining the presentation.
steps.say: The Budapest criteria confirm CRPS: pain out of proportion to the injury, with symptoms in three of four categories and objective signs in at least two categories: sensory, vasomotor, sudomotor, and motor or trophic.

left.title: Budapest Clinical Criteria
points: Patient reports symptoms in 3 of 4 groups
Clinician observes signs in 2 of 4 groups

steps.tx: **Spotty osteopenia** on plain radiographs represents a classic diagnostic radiographic sign of complex regional pain syndrome. Radiographs of the affected hand or foot display patchy, patchy ground-glass subchondral and metaphyseal demineralization, colloquially known as Sudeck atrophy. In triple-phase technetium-99m bone scintigraphy, the delayed mineral phase demonstrates diffuse, asymmetrical, periarticular tracer hyperfixation across multiple small joints of the involved extremity, confirming heightened bone turnover driven by neurovascular shunting.
steps.say: Plain X-rays show spotty, patchy osteopenia in the small bones of the hand or foot, known as Sudeck atrophy. A triple-phase bone scan shows diffuse periarticular tracer pooling across all small joints.

vis.title: Imaging and Diagnostic Modalities in CRPS
rows: High sensitivity in early warm phase (<6 months)
Normal in type 1; focal axonal defect in type 2

steps.tx: **Physical therapy** and early active functional rehabilitation form the mandatory foundation of treatment for complex regional pain syndrome. Graded motor imagery, mirror therapy, and gentle desensitization techniques using progressively coarse fabrics rewire maladaptive cortical representations and diminish central allodynia. Immobility and prolonged splinting must be rigorously avoided because joint rest accelerates muscular atrophy, tendon adhesions, and irreversible fibrous contracture of the limb.
steps.say: Physical therapy and active mobilization are the most important treatments. Mirror therapy and graded motor imagery help rewire the brain. Prolonged casting and splinting must be avoided because immobility makes CRPS worse.

nodes.label: Graded Imagery
nodes.sub: Left-right motor recognition and mirror therapy

nodes.label: Active Loading
nodes.sub: Gentle weight-bearing and functional daily use

nodes.label: Interventional Blocks
nodes.sub: Sympathetic nerve block or spinal cord stimulator

steps.tx: **Sympathetic ganglion blocks** provide targeted diagnostic confirmation and therapeutic interruption of sympathetically maintained pain pathways. For upper extremity disease, a local anaesthetic blockade of the cervical sympathetic chain at the stellate ganglion (C6 level) induces temporary Horner syndrome, warming of the hand, and dramatic pain relief. For lower extremity involvement, a lumbar sympathetic block targeting the L2 to L4 prevertebral sympathetic ganglia breaks the autonomic reflex arc, facilitating intensive physical therapy.
steps.say: Sympathetic nerve blocks target the autonomic reflex loop: stellate ganglion block for the arm and lumbar sympathetic block for the leg. Successful blockade relieves pain and warms the limb, opening a window for physical therapy.

vis.title: Interventional Sympathetic Procedures in CRPS
rows: Lower limb skin temperature rises >=2.0 deg C
Refractory CRPS failing medical and block therapy
Bier block with bretylium or lidocaine
Temporary chemical sympathectomy of distal limb

steps.tx: **Vitamin C** administered at a daily oral dose of five hundred milligrams for fifty consecutive days following distal radius fractures significantly reduces the incidence of complex regional pain syndrome. In prospective randomized trials, ascorbic acid acts as an effective free radical scavenger and antioxidant, dampening post-traumatic microvascular reperfusion injury and neurogenic inflammation. Routine prophylactic vitamin C is now widely recommended following wrist fractures and foot trauma.
steps.say: Oral vitamin C at 500 milligrams daily for fifty days following a Colles wrist fracture prevents CRPS by scavenging free radicals and dampening neurogenic inflammation. It is a simple, proven prophylaxis.

left.title: Prophylactic Vitamin C Protocol
points: Reduces CRPS risk by over fifty percent

right.title: Established Disease Pharmacotherapy
points: Short-course oral prednisone for acute edema
